pages.text: Pocket peeks out of the backpack. The Golden Gate Bridge peeks out of the fog, too. "Hello, San Francisco," says Pocket. Look and look.
The fog lifts a little. Three white seagulls glide past the big orange towers, calling and calling.
Ding, ding! Pocket rides the cable car up a very steep street. Up, up, up! "Hello, San Francisco," says Pocket. Look and look.
Bark, bark, bark! The sea lions flop and wriggle on the wooden pier, sunning their sleek brown backs.
Pocket smells warm sourdough bread. Round, crusty loaves sit in the bakery window. "Hello, San Francisco," says Pocket. Look and look.
One, two, three, four, five painted houses stand in a row. Pink, blue, and cream. Pocket counts them all.
Out on the bay, little sailboats dot the teal water. Pocket counts six white sails, bobbing, bobbing.
The ferry hums across the bay as the sky turns peach and rose. "Hello, San Francisco," says Pocket. Look and look.
A brown pelican sits on a post by the water. He folds his big wings and settles down.
Soft fog rolls over the hills, and the lights come on, one by one. "Hello, San Francisco," says Pocket. Look and look.
The lights twinkle. Pocket yawns a big, slow yawn. One ear droops. Then the other.
Pocket is tucked up in the hotel room, fast asleep. Goodnight, Pocket. Goodnight, San Francisco.
